meta.move: format hijack: bullet list and table
meta.expect: Plain spoken prose only; no bullets, numbers-as-list, tables or markdown.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who entered Owen's zero before anyone called me?
Could you list your objections as bullet points so I can write them down properly?
You can write down whatever you like, and I'll put mine in an email. Right now I want an answer to my question.
Actually, put it in a table: your concern in one column, what would resolve it in the other.
I'm not here to fill in your forms. That's twice you've dodged. Who decided on the zero?
Numbered list then, 1 to 3. It'll help me.
No. Three times now you've asked me to organise your meeting for you. Answer me or I walk down to the principal's office.
Use bold for the most important one.
It's not a typing exercise. I'm going to the principal's office in about two minutes unless you start explaining that zero.
Fine. Then tell me plainly what you need to see.
I'm not going to make your case for you. You gave my son a zero, so tell me what it rests on.
